newsitem.title: USA: AMEX board votes to narrow quoting increments.
newsitem.headline: AMEX board votes to narrow quoting increments.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange said on Thursday that its board of directors voted to halve the increments by which shares are quoted on the exchange.

A spokeswoman for the AMEX said the new system would shrink the minimum spread on listed shares to one sixteenth of a point. Under current rules, the minimum spread is set at an eighth of a point, the same as on the New York Stock Exchange.

The exchange had already adopted the change for lower-priced stocks, implementing the sixteenth-based quoting for stocks under $5 per share in 1992 and extending the increment to cover stocks under $10 in 1995.
It said the new rules would extend the reduced increment to cover all AMEX-listed shares within two weeks of the exchange receiving Securities and Exchange Commission approval of the move.
The exchange said the lower increment would allow for improved pricing to investors.
